messages.subject: Issue with small number variable
parts:
Hello list,

I am modelling the probability of recaptures from a mosquito MR experiment. My model has a binomial likelihood, default INLA priors and a spatio-temporal structure, here is my R code to run it:

outinla<-inla(pa ~ 1 + sex + dist ... + dayfromrel f(parid, model="bym2", graph=MAD.adj) + f(parid_g, dayfromrel, model = "iid",constr=TRUE) ,family="binomial",data=iso4m, Ntrials=daily_abundance,control.compute=list(waic = TRUE))

Now I want to transform "dist" variable (which represents the distance of recapture from release point) using a negative exponential kernel and use the transformed distance as a predictor. The literature on the topic suggests that this should improve model predictions.

The issue is that the transformed distance (range: 5.74e-08-1.14e-06) is 6-8 order of magnitude smaller than the other predictors and when I add it to the model, the posterior probability distribution for its model term does not make much sense, due to a huge standard deviation (mean=0.0136, sd=31.6228). 

If I substitute the variable with a vector of 0's, the sd deviation of the posterior distribution remains the same.

Is there an explanation for this behaviour? How I can add this variable and obtain a reasonable estimate of its posterior distribution?

Thanks,
Matteo

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issue with small number variable
parts:
Hi,
The sd=31.6228 is the prior sd (31.6228^2 = 1000 which is the prior variance), meaning that your model is not informative about this parameter.

Try to rescale the dist covariate and only fit this, to see what the effect is in a simple model.

Regards,
Haakon

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issue with small number variable
parts:
It is known that the prior of beta is N(0, 1000) which means that the X-covariate-values cannot be too small. But you should still not get the results you got!

The covariate values are not read as 0. But the matrix algebra might be less stable with these small values.

Do you have time to make a small code example replicating the problem, so that we can look at it?
(Please also update your version of INLA first.)

Best,
Haakon

#Dataset
data=as.data.frame(matrix(c(0,0,0,0,0,1,3,1,2,2,1,1,2,1,2,20,25,12,11,1,20,20,6,10,8,3,4,10,5,4,500,300,140,600,200,160,200,150,130,160,120,98,45,20,35),ncol=3))
names(data) <- c("s","trials","distance")

#Exponential power kernel

data$expkd<-((y/(2*pi*(x^2)*base::gamma(2/y)))*exp(-(data$distance^y/(x^y)))) 
data$expkd_t<-((y/(2*pi*(x^2)*base::gamma(2/y)))*exp(-(data$distance^y/(x^y))))*10000

m2<-inla(s ~ 1 + expkd_t, data=data, Ntrials=trials,family="binomial") # correct sd


Matteo

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issue with small number variable
parts:
See the code below. The trick is to use the exact same prior (model) in both cases to get the same results:

Note that NEITHER of these are recommended options. What I would recommend is same/similar to what you use as m2:
>> data$expkd_t<-((y/(2*pi*(x^2)*base::gamma(2/y)))*exp(-(data$distance^y/(x^y))))*1E5


-----

#Dataset
data=as.data.frame(matrix(c(0,0,0,0,0,1,3,1,2,2,1,1,2,1,2,20,25,12,11,1,20,20,6,10,8,3,4,10,5,4,500,300,140,600,200,160,200,150,130,160,120,98,45,20,35),ncol=3))
names(data) <- c("s","trials","distance")


#Exponential power kernel
x=230;y=3
data$expkd<-((y/(2*pi*(x^2)*base::gamma(2/y)))*exp(-(data$distance^y/(x^y))))
data$expkd_t<-((y/(2*pi*(x^2)*base::gamma(2/y)))*exp(-(data$distance^y/(x^y))))*10000

#Models

m1<-inla(s ~ 1 + expkd, data=data, Ntrials=trials,family="binomial",
         control.fixed = list(prec = 1E-3),
         control.predictor = list(compute=T)) # ppd sd to the prior sd
m2<-inla(s ~ 1 + expkd_t, data=data, Ntrials=trials,family="binomial",
         control.fixed = list(prec = 1E5),
         control.predictor = list(compute=T)) # correct sd
# Using 1E5 = 1E-3 * (1E-4)^(-2)
summary(m1)
summary(m2)

## Similar
summary(m1$summary.fixed$`0.5quant`[2]*data$expkd)
summary(m2$summary.fixed$`0.5quant`[2]*data$expkd_t)

summary(m1$summary.linear.predictor$mean)
summary(m2$summary.linear.predictor$mean)

plot(m1$summary.linear.predictor$mean, data$s/data$trials)
plot(m2$summary.linear.predictor$mean, data$s/data$trials)
-----
